sentences.en: Cannon to right of them.
sentences.zh: 大炮在他们右侧轰鸣。

sentences.en: Cannon to left of them.
sentences.zh: 大炮在他们左侧轰鸣。

sentences.en: Cannon in front of them, volleyed and thundered.
sentences.zh: 大炮在他们正面，齐射且雷霆万钧。

sentences.en: Stormed at with shot and shell.
sentences.zh: 枪林弹雨如暴风般袭来。

sentences.en: Boldly they rode and well.
sentences.zh: 他们英勇无畏地驰骋。

sentences.en: Into the jaws of death.
sentences.zh: 冲向死亡的巨口。

sentences.en: Into the mouth of hell rode the 600.
sentences.zh: 六百壮士冲进地狱之门。

sentences.en: So that was Alfred Law Tennyson's famous poem, The Charge of the Light Brigade,
sentences.zh: 以上便是阿尔弗雷德·劳·丁尼生的著名诗篇《轻骑兵的冲锋》，

sentences.en: written as we heard last time in 1854 to commemorate the most glorious and heroic debacle in British military history.
sentences.zh: 正如我们上次所听到的，这首诗写于 1854 年，旨在纪念英国军事史上那场最辉煌也最英勇的惨败。

sentences.en: I don't think any other country talks of a glorious debacle with a relish that we do.
sentences.zh: 我觉得没有哪个国家能像我们这样，带着一种津津乐道的心态去谈论一场辉煌的惨败。

sentences.en: Because so much winning, Tom.
sentences.zh: 因为我们赢了太多，汤姆。

sentences.en: So much winning.
sentences.zh: 赢了太多。

sentences.en: So we are building up in this mighty series, To the Charge of the Light Brigade.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们这档气势恢弘的系列节目中，我们正在为《轻骑兵的冲锋》做铺垫。

sentences.en: We've been talking about some of the personalities involved in the build-up to this moment on the 25th of October, 1854,
sentences.zh: 我们一直在探讨在 1854 年 10 月 25 日这一决定性时刻来临前参与其中的一些重要人物，

sentences.en: when the cream of the British light cavalry launched this suicidal assault on an entire battery of Russian guns, the jaws of death.
sentences.zh: 当时英国轻骑兵的精英们对俄军的整座炮兵阵地发起了这起无异于自杀的冲锋，直入死亡的巨口。

sentences.en: Tom, in the first episode, we were talking about the steps by which Britain and France advanced to war with Russia.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，在第一集中，我们讨论了英国和法国走向对俄战争的各个步骤。

sentences.en: So they declared war on the 28th of March, 1854.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们在 1854 年 3 月 28 日正式宣战。

sentences.en: And just remind us what this is all about.
sentences.zh: 请再提醒我们一下，这一切究竟是为了什么。

sentences.en: What's the goal here?
sentences.zh: 这里的目标是什么？

sentences.en: So the goal of the British and French is to prevent Russia from dismembering the Ottoman Empire and capturing Constantinople,
sentences.zh: 英法两国的目标是阻止俄罗斯肢解奥斯曼帝国并占领君士坦丁堡，

sentences.en: because both countries feel that this would threaten their vital interests in the EaSt.
sentences.zh: 因为两国都认为这会威胁到他们在东方（the East）的核心利益。

sentences.en: The Tsar thinks that he can co-opt Britain into the project of dismembering the Ottoman Empire.
sentences.zh: 沙皇认为他可以把英国拉拢到肢解奥斯曼帝国的计划中来。

sentences.en: So early in 1854, he'd talk to the British ambassador about this and dismiss the Ottoman Empire as the sick man of Europe.
sentences.zh: 因此在 1854 年初，他曾与英国大使谈及此事，并将奥斯曼帝国贬低为“欧洲病夫”。

sentences.en: And he wants to put the sick man out of his misery.
sentences.zh: 他想让这位“病夫”彻底解脱。

sentences.en: But the British and the French don't want this at all, because they would much rather have a sick man in charge of Constantinople than the Gendarme of Europe,
sentences.zh: 但英法两国对此坚决不同意，因为比起被称为“欧洲宪兵”的沙皇，他们宁愿让一个“病夫”来主政君士坦丁堡，

sentences.en: which is the nickname that Nicholas has.
sentences.zh: 尼古拉一世恰好就有这个绰号。

sentences.en: He's seen as a much more effective, efficient figure.
sentences.zh: 在人们眼中，他是一个效率极高、作风强悍的人物。

sentences.en: And so therefore, they want to keep him at bay.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们想要将他遏制住。

sentences.en: And Britain, even before the declaration of war on the 28th of March, 1854, the government had been preparing for the outbreak of full hostilities.
sentences.zh: 早在 1854 年 3 月 28 日正式宣战之前，英国政府就已经在为全面敌对状态的爆发做准备了。

sentences.en: So as early as September 1853, as we heard in the previous episode, the Royal Navy had sent a flotilla to Constantinople up into the Bosphorus.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在上一集中听到的那样，早在 1853 年 9 月，英国皇家海军就派遣了一支分舰队前往君士坦丁堡，驶入博斯普鲁斯海峡。

sentences.en: And its commander was a chap called Vice Admiral James Dundas, which is a tremendous name for Royal Navy Admiral.
sentences.zh: 其指挥官是一位名叫詹姆斯·邓达斯的海军中将，对于皇家海军上将来说，这绝对是一个威风凛凛的名字。

sentences.en: He's very old school.
sentences.zh: 他非常符合传统老派作风。

sentences.en: So he is a veteran of the Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 他是拿破仑战争的老兵。

sentences.en: He's tremendously grand.
sentences.zh: 他极其气派威严。

sentences.en: He's tremendously bald.
sentences.zh: 他极其光头（指秃顶）。

sentences.en: Um, so kind of redolent of the age of Nelson, but the flotilla that he commands is definitely not old school.
sentences.zh: 嗯，多少有点纳尔逊时代的遗风，但他所指挥的分舰队绝对不是老派风格。

sentences.en: Um, it's an absolutely bristling display of naval strength, 16 warships, 645 guns, very intimidating.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这展现出了海军绝对强悍的实力：16艘军舰、645门大炮，极具威慑力。

sentences.en: And by January, Dundas's squadron is operating openly in the Black Sea, which the Russians, for understandable reasons, see as their own lake.
sentences.zh: 到了 1 月，邓达斯的舰队已经公开在黑海活动，处于可以理解的原因，俄国人将黑海视作他们自己的内湖。

sentences.en: And so they demand that the British withdraw and Dundas refuses.
sentences.zh: 因此他们要求英方撤离，而邓达斯拒绝了。

sentences.en: Um, and he's able to do that because he's confident that they massively outgun the Russians.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他之所以能这么做，是因为他确信他们的火力远超俄军。

sentences.en: So that in a sense, although it's not been officially declared, the naval war between Britain and Russia has begun in the Crimea.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，尽管尚未正式宣战，英国和俄罗斯在克里米亚的海战已经打响了。

sentences.en: And it is increasingly clear to the British government that there is going to be a war by land as well.
sentences.zh: 英国政府也越来越清楚地意识到，陆战也将不可避免地爆发。

sentences.en: And if this land war breaks out, then that will be the responsibility of someone we met at the end of the last episode.
sentences.zh: 如果这场陆战爆发，那将由我们在上一集末尾介绍过的一位人物负责。

sentences.en: And this was a chap called Viscount Harding, who had recently been appointed as commander in chief of the army in succession to the Duke of Wellington, who had died in 1852.
sentences.zh: 这个人就是哈丁子爵，他最近被任命为陆军总司令，接替了于 1852 年逝世的威灵顿公爵。

sentences.en: And just to give him a shout out, he is probably the ablest man we will be meeting in the series.
sentences.zh: 顺便表扬他一下，他可能是我们在本系列中将遇到的最有能力的人。

sentences.en: I mean, that's not a huge compliment, but I mean, it's better than, better than nothing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这算不上什么极高的赞誉，但总比没有强、比没有强。

sentences.en: And this is a guy who his entire career has seen the functioning of British greatness up close.
sentences.zh: 这家伙的整个职业生涯都近距离见证了英国伟大力量的运转。

sentences.en: He knows what it is that makes British geopolitical muscle what it is.
sentences.zh: 他深知究竟是什么造就了英国的地缘政治实力。

sentences.en: So he's a hero of the Peninsular War, the war fought by Sir Arthur Wellesley, as he was before he became the Duke of Wellington in Iberia against Napoleon's armies.
sentences.zh: 他是半岛战争的英雄。半岛战争是由阿瑟·韦尔斯利（即后来成为威灵顿公爵之前的他）在伊比利亚半岛率领，对抗拿破仑军队的战争。

sentences.en: Then in 1815, he'd served as the liaison officer with the Prussians in the war against Napoleon in the Waterloo campaign.
sentences.zh: 随后在 1815 年，他在滑铁卢战役中担任反拿破仑战争中与普鲁士军队的联络官。

sentences.en: And he'd fought at the Battle of Nini, which he'd lost a hand.
sentences.zh: 他在利尼战役中作战，并在战斗中失去了一只手。

sentences.en: And there's a lot of kind of bodily dismemberment in this series.
sentences.zh: 这个系列里有各种各样的身体残缺情节。

sentences.en: Wellington had fought a duel in 1829, a bit like the Earl of Cardigan did.
sentences.zh: 威灵顿在 1829 年曾进行过一场决斗，有点像卡迪根伯爵那样。

sentences.en: And Harding had been his second in that duel.
sentences.zh: 而哈丁在那场决斗中担任他的副手（秒表/见证人）。

sentences.en: So that was good.
sentences.zh: 所以那挺不错。

sentences.en: And then he'd been appointed governor general of India.
sentences.zh: 后来他被任命为印度总督。

sentences.en: And he'd served there 1844 to 1848.
sentences.zh: 他于 1844 年至 1848 年在那里任职。

sentences.en: And so he shares in this widespread anxiety that you were talking about in the previous episode, Dominic,
sentences.zh: 因此，他也分担了你在上一集中谈到的那种普遍焦虑，多米尼克，

sentences.en: worries that the movement of Russian power into Central Asia might come to threaten the British position in India.
sentences.zh: 人们担心俄罗斯势力的南下进入中亚可能会威胁到英国在印度的地位。

sentences.en: So he is anxious about the claws of the Russian bear reaching southwards towards the Khyber Pass.
sentences.zh: 因此，他对于俄罗斯熊的爪子向南伸向开伯尔山口感到忧心忡忡。

sentences.en: And then by the standards of the mid-19th century Victorian army, Harding is something of a moderniser, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 以 19 世纪中期维多利亚时代陆军的标准来看，哈丁算得上是一位革新者，对吧？

sentences.en: So he's getting them to do something unheard of, which is field manoeuvres.
sentences.zh: 所以他让他们做了一件前所未闻的事情，那就是野外战术演习。

sentences.en: So people had never done this before.
sentences.zh: 人们以前从未做过这种事。

sentences.en: Well, they'd done it in the Napoleonic Wars, but they hadn't done it since.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他们在拿破仑战争中做过，但自那以后就没再搞过了。

sentences.en: And this takes place in the summer of 1853.
sentences.zh: 这发生在 1853 年的夏天。

sentences.en: So, you know, summer before the declaration of war.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，是在宣战前的那个夏天。

sentences.en: And he'd arranged for 10,000 men from different regiments to meet up on this field in Surrey.
sentences.zh: 他安排了来自不同团的 1,0000 名士兵在萨里的这片田野上会合。

sentences.en: And it's the first field manoeuvres that the British army has staged since the Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 这是自拿破仑战争以来英国陆军首次举行野外战术演习。

sentences.en: And I think it is an indication that with Wellington dead, it is time for a new age.
sentences.zh: 我认为这表明，随着威灵顿的逝世，是时候迎来一个新时代了。

sentences.en: And Harding is absolutely happy to step up to the plate and try and introduce this.
sentences.zh: 而哈丁绝对乐意挺身而出，尝试引入这一切。

sentences.en: And the other thing that he does, which will prove to have considerable consequences in the Crimean War,
sentences.zh: 他做的另一件事，将在克里米亚战争中产生深远的影响，

sentences.en: is that he has been pushing for the wholesale adoption by the army of a lethal new rifle, the Minier, which, as its name suggests, isn't actually British, but French.
sentences.zh: 那就是他一直在推动陆军全面列装一种威力巨大新型步枪——米涅步枪（the Minié）。正如其名，它其实不是英国的，而是法国的。

sentences.en: And it's been invented in 1849, so only four years previously, by a captain in the French army.
sentences.zh: 它是在 1849 年，也就是仅仅四年前，由一名法军上尉发明的。

sentences.en: So that's, this guy was called Minier, so hence the name of the rifle.
sentences.zh: 所以，这家伙名叫米涅，这也是该步枪名称的由来。

sentences.en: And it's much longer range than a musket.
sentences.zh: 它的射程比滑膛枪远得多。

sentences.en: It's much more accurate, and it has much greater precision.
sentences.zh: 它准确度高得多，精度也大得多。

sentences.en: And it's Harding who's spotted its potential when the French military high command haven't.
sentences.zh: 正是哈丁在法国军方高层尚未察觉时，就发现了它的潜力。

sentences.en: So the French won't end up adopting it until 1857.
sentences.zh: 所以法国人直到 1857 年才最终装备它。

sentences.en: And Harding is saying, yeah, we've got to have this.
sentences.zh: 而哈丁则说，行吧，我们必须拥有这个。

sentences.en: It's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: And so throughout the summer of 1853 and into 1854, British regiments are starting to be issued with this rifle.
sentences.zh: 因此，在 1853 年整个夏天一直到 1854 年，英国各团开始配发这种步枪。

sentences.en: So yeah, I mean, he's a clear-sighted, proactive man, and exactly the kind of man who, prior to the official declaration of war, is absolutely making preparations for the conflict.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我的意思是，他是一个目光敏锐、积极主动的人，也正是那种在正式宣战前就为冲突做好充分准备的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He's the commander-in-chief, so he's not going to command the army in the Crimea.
sentences.zh: 他是总司令，所以他不会亲自去克里米亚指挥军队。

sentences.en: He needs to send, you know, somebody in his stead.
sentences.zh: 他需要派，你知道的，另一个人去代替他。

sentences.en: And this, so clearly he's not going to choose somebody who's earned it through his own efforts.
sentences.zh: 因此，显然他不会选择那些靠自身努力挣得这一职位的人。

sentences.en: I mean, that would be absolutely ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那绝对太荒谬了。

sentences.en: No, that would be ludicrous.
sentences.zh: 不，那太滑稽了。

sentences.en: It would be ludicrous.
sentences.zh: 那简直滑稽透顶。

sentences.en: So he's going to choose somebody, well, he's, let's not put too far on a point, he's going to choose Lord Waglan, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以他会选择一个人，好吧，咱们话休啰嗦，他要选择拉格朗勋爵（Lord Raglan），不是吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think it will stun listeners to know that the person appointed to the command of the British army in Crimea is going to be another lord.
sentences.zh: 我想这会让听众们大吃一惊：被任命指挥克里米亚英军的人竟然又是另一位勋爵。

sentences.en: I mean, who would have seen that coming?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁能料到这一点呢？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is the first Baron Waglan, Fitzroy Somerset, the first Lord Baron Waglan.
sentences.zh: 这位就是第一代拉格朗男爵，菲茨罗伊·萨默塞特，第一代拉格朗男爵。

sentences.en: But actually, Waglan, you know, he's actually very much Harding's kind of chap.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，拉格朗，你知道的，他其实非常对哈丁的脾胃。

sentences.en: He's cut from very similar cloth.
sentences.zh: 他们俩是一丘之貉。

sentences.en: So like Harding, Waglan had fought at Wellington's side in the Peninsular War.
sentences.zh: 和哈丁一样，拉格朗曾在半岛战争中与威灵顿并肩作战。

sentences.en: And like Harding, he had lost a bodily appendage in the Waterloo campaign.
sentences.zh: 和哈丁一样，他在滑铁卢战役中失去了一处身体附属器官。

sentences.en: And he had lost his appendage actually at the Battle of Waterloo itself, where he was serving on Wellington's staff.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他正是在滑铁卢战役本身中失去了他的手臂，当时他在威灵顿的参谋部任职。

sentences.en: He'd been shot in the arm.
sentences.zh: 他的手臂中枪了。

sentences.en: The arm needed to be amputated.
sentences.zh: 这条胳膊需要截肢。

sentences.en: And this was performed without anesthetic.
sentences.zh: 而且是在没有麻醉的情况下进行的手术。

sentences.en: Waglan gave barely a peep.
sentences.zh: 拉格朗几乎连一声都没吭。

sentences.en: So he is incredibly tough, incredibly stoical.
sentences.zh: 所以他极其坚韧，极其坚忍。

sentences.en: And after his arm had been sawn off, and it was about to be thrown away, he demanded indignantly, here, don't take that arm away until I have taken the ring off the finger.
sentences.zh: 当他的胳膊被锯掉、正要被扔掉时，他愤怒地质问：“喂，先把那只胳膊放下，等我把手指上的戒指取下来再拿走。”

sentences.en: And the ring had been a gift from his wife.
sentences.zh: 那枚戒指是他妻子送给他的礼物。

sentences.en: And so he wanted to make sure that that wasn't loSt.
sentences.zh: 因此他要确保那枚戒指没有丢失。

sentences.en: Oh, that's a nice story.
sentences.zh: 哦，真是个不错的故事。

sentences.en: So he's very stoical.
sentences.zh: 所以他非常坚忍。

sentences.en: He's a very brave man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常勇敢的人。

sentences.en: And he's seen a lot of action.
sentences.zh: 而且他经历过许多战事。

sentences.en: So you'd think he'd be ideally suited to this.
sentences.zh: 所以你会觉得他是胜任此职的绝佳人选。

sentences.en: The problem is that for pretty much the entirety of his career, so from 1808, when he'd first
sentences.zh: 问题在于，在几乎他的整个职业生涯中——也就是说，从 1808 年他第一次

sentences.en: gone out to serve on the staff of Sir Arthur Wellesley, as the Duke of Wellington was originally
sentences.zh: 前往阿瑟·韦尔斯利（即最初的威灵顿公爵）在葡萄牙的参谋部任职开始，

sentences.en: in Portugal, right up to the death of Wellington in 1852, he'd basically always been the deputy to Wellington.
sentences.zh: 一直到 1852 年威灵顿逝世，他基本上一直都是威灵顿的副手。

sentences.en: He'd always been the number two.
sentences.zh: 他一直是老二。

sentences.en: And so his talents reflect this.
sentences.zh: 因此，他的才能也正体现了这一点。

sentences.en: His talents are less those of a commander than of a diplomat.
sentences.zh: 与其说他具备指挥官的才能，倒不如说他更具备外交官的才华。

sentences.en: He's a man who hates conflict, who has incredible resources of charm, which he is always deploying.
sentences.zh: 他是一个讨厌冲突的人，拥有令人惊叹的迷人魅力，并且总是在施展这种魅力。

sentences.en: He's like the kind of benignant capitalist who, at the end of a Dickens novel, solves everyone's probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他就像狄更斯小说结尾那种慈祥的资本家，能帮所有人解决难题。

sentences.en: All right, a sort of Mr. Cheerable kind of person or something.
sentences.zh: 没错，有点像切罗布尔（Mr. Cheeryble）那种类型的人之类的。

sentences.en: Yes, he exudes a kind of jovial sense of benignity.
sentences.zh: 是的，他散发着一种随和友善、慈祥温和的气质。

sentences.en: And people instinctively like him.
sentences.zh: 人们会不由自主地喜欢他。

sentences.en: And I think if you had met him in civilian costume, you would never have it.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你穿着便服遇见他，你绝不会

sentences.en: You'd never put him down as a military man.
sentences.zh: 绝不会把他当作一个军人。

sentences.en: So to quote Cecil Woodham Smith, whose wonderful book on the charge of the light brigade I read when I was very young, and it gave me a devotion to the whole story.
sentences.zh: 借用塞西尔·伍德姆-史密斯的话来说——我年轻时读过她关于轻骑兵冲锋的精彩著作，正是这本书让我对整个故事魂牵梦绕。

sentences.en: She said of Raglan, his beautiful face looked like the face of an ecclesiastic, a cardinal of
sentences.zh: 她这样评价拉格朗：“他那漂亮的脸庞看起来像是一个神职人员的面孔，也许是一位文艺复兴时期的红衣主教，

sentences.en: the Renaissance, perhaps, urbane, subtle, diplomatic, ruthlessness, determination were wanting.
sentences.zh: 温文尔雅、精明含蓄、长于外交，却唯独缺乏冷酷无情与坚定果断。”

sentences.en: And in the 1968 film, I don't know if you've seen, have you seen that?
sentences.zh: 在 1968 年的电影里，我不知道你有没有看过，你看过那部电影吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, years and years ago.
sentences.zh: 看过，很多年前了。

sentences.en: Trevor Howard plays Cardigan, and Raglan is played by John Gielgud.
sentences.zh: 特雷弗·霍华德饰演卡迪根，而拉格朗则由约翰·吉尔古德饰演。

sentences.en: And that is perfect casting.
sentences.zh: 那简直是完美的选角。

sentences.en: Absolutely perfect casting.
sentences.zh: 绝对完美的选角。

sentences.en: Charming, but perhaps a little ineffectual.
sentences.zh: 迷人，但或许有些华而不实。

sentences.en: That's the decision that has to be made.
sentences.zh: 这是必须要作出的决定。

sentences.en: Is he qualified to take on command?
sentences.zh: 他有资格接任指挥官吗？

sentences.en: Is he ready to step out from the shadow of the Iron Duke?
sentences.zh: 他准备好走出铁公爵的阴影了吗？

sentences.en: And actually, when Harding first proposes Raglan as commander for the Eastern Expedition
sentences.zh: 事实上，当哈丁首次向英国内阁战争大臣纽卡斯尔公爵提议

sentences.en: to the Duke of Newcastle, who is the Secretary for War in the British Cabinet, Newcastle says, oh, really?
sentences.zh: 由拉格兰担任远征东方联军的指挥官时，纽卡斯尔说，哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, isn't he a bit of a number two?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他难道不是有点像个副手吗？

sentences.en: You know, he has no experience as a field commander.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他没有任何野战指挥官的经验。

sentences.en: Are you absolutely certain?
sentences.zh: 你完全确定吗？

sentences.en: But, you know, a week passes and another.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，一周又一周过去了。

sentences.en: It's obvious that they've been discussing it.
sentences.zh: 很明显，他们一直在讨论这件事。

sentences.en: And they think, yeah, actually, probably he is the man.
sentences.zh: 然后他们想，是的，实际上，他大概就是合适的人选。

sentences.en: And on the 21st of February, Raglan is duly appointed by the British government general officer commanding the forces east of Malta.
sentences.zh: 2月21日，拉格兰正式被英国政府任命为马耳他以东军队的陆军中将兼司令。

sentences.en: So why?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么呢？

sentences.en: Why has Newcastle changed his mind?
sentences.zh: 为什么纽卡斯尔改变了主意？

sentences.en: Why is Harding keen to see Raglan take up the post?
sentences.zh: 为什么哈丁渴望看到拉格兰接任这个职务？

sentences.en: I think undoubtedly there is a lack of imagination there.
sentences.zh: 我认为毫无疑问，那里缺乏想象力。

sentences.en: So Harding is, you know, I mean, he's a product of his class.
sentences.zh: 所以哈丁，你知道的，我的意思是，他是他那个阶层的产物。

sentences.en: He's not immune to snobbery himself.
sentences.zh: 他自己也并非对势利免疫。

sentences.en: And although there are definitely officers in the British Army who have the requisite experience, who have fought battles, who know what it's like to command an army under gunfire,
sentences.zh: 尽管英国陆军中确实有这样的军官，他们拥有必要的经验，打过仗，知道在炮火下指挥军队是什么滋味，

sentences.en: it never crosses Harding's mind to consider these officers.
sentences.zh: 但哈丁从未想过要考虑这些军官。

sentences.en: And the ablest of them is a man called Sir Colin Campbell, who is 61 years old by this point.
sentences.zh: 其中能力最强的是一个叫科林·坎贝尔爵士的人，此时他已经61岁了。

sentences.en: So pretty elderly.
sentences.zh: 所以年龄相当大了。

sentences.en: He's very grizzled.
sentences.zh: 他饱经风霜。

sentences.en: He's a battle-hardened Scot.
sentences.zh: 他是一位久经沙场的苏格兰人。

sentences.en: And he'd had decades of experience in India in particular, and he'd won a brilliant name for himself in the conquest of the Punjab.
sentences.zh: 他在印度有几十年的经验，尤其是在征服旁遮普期间，他为自己赢得了极高的声誉。

sentences.en: But the problem is, and this is a problem for Harding as for everyone else in the upper echelons of the British Army and the British government, he's the son of a Guasgo carpenter.
sentences.zh: 但问题是——这对哈丁来说是个问题，对英国陆军和英国政府高层的其他人来说也是个问题——他是格拉斯哥木匠的儿子。

sentences.en: You can't have the son of a Guasgo carpenter in charge of the army.
sentences.zh: 你不能让一个格拉斯哥木匠的儿子来掌管军队。

sentences.en: And he'd spent most of his career in India, as we've said.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，他职业生涯的大部分时间都在印度度过。

sentences.en: And he doesn't have the money.
sentences.zh: 而且他没有钱。

sentences.en: He doesn't have the patrons.
sentences.zh: 他没有后台。

sentences.en: You know, he just doesn't have the breeding or the class.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他就是没有家世或阶层。

sentences.en: So there's no way that even though he's obviously the ideal man for the job, he's incredibly, you know, as we will see, a brilliant, brilliant commander.
sentences.zh: 所以没有办法，尽管他显然是这份工作的理想人选，正如我们稍后会看到的，他是一个极其、极其出色的指挥官。

sentences.en: You can't have that class of chap in charge.
sentences.zh: 你不能让那种阶层的人来掌权。

sentences.en: And so Campbell, by this point, is still only a colonel.
sentences.zh: 因此，直到这个时候，坎贝尔仍然只是一名上校。

sentences.en: And it's unthinkable that he could be promoted over his military and social superiors.
sentences.zh: 让人无法想象的是，他竟然可以凌驾于他的军事和社会上级之上获得晋升。

sentences.en: And so instead, he is given a command in the expedition.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为替代，他在远征军中得到了一个指挥权。

sentences.en: He's given command of three Highland units, so the Highland Brigade.
sentences.zh: 他被委任指挥三个高地部队，也就是高地旅。

sentences.en: And as we will see, Campbell in the Crimea will cover himself with glory, but not as commander of chief.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，坎贝尔在克里米亚将声名大噪，但并非作为总司令。

sentences.en: But to be fair to the British High Command and to Harding and to Newcastle,
sentences.zh: 但平心而论，站在英国最高指挥部、哈丁以及纽卡斯尔的角度来看，

sentences.en: I think there is a second reason why the British cabinet decides that Raglan, after all, is their man.
sentences.zh: 我认为英国内阁决定拉格兰毕竟是他们的人，还有第二个原因。

sentences.en: And firstly, they're not 100% sure at this point that there is going to be a war.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们此时并不百分之百确定会爆发战争。

sentences.en: I mean, it's still possible that there won't be.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，仍然有可能不会爆发。

sentences.en: And even if there is a war, actually, Raglan's talents as a diplomat are going to prove incredibly useful.
sentences.zh: 即便真的爆发了战争，事实上，拉格兰作为外交官的才能也将证明是极其有用的。

sentences.en: Because obviously, he's going to have to go out to the east, to Constantinople, and there he will have to liaise with the Turk.
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，他将不得不前往东方，去君士坦丁堡，在那里他必须与土耳其人进行联络。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone likes to liaise with the Turk, don't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每个人都喜欢与土耳其人打交道，不是吗？

sentences.en: The Foreign Secretary has taken Raglan to one side and has warned him that in his dealings with the Turk,
sentences.zh: 外交大臣曾把拉格兰拉到一边，警告他在与土耳其人打交道时，

sentences.en: he should be warned that the Turk has been, and I quote, enfeebled by abominations.
sentences.zh: 应该当心土耳其人已经——我引述一下——“被各种恶习严重削弱”。

sentences.en: And what these abominations are, no one actually says.
sentences.zh: 而这些恶习究竟是什么，没有人真正明说。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: But it's something to bear in mind.
sentences.zh: 但这是需要牢记的一点。

sentences.en: And so it's important, you know, Raglan needs to go out and deal with all this.
sentences.zh: 所以这很重要，你知道的，拉格兰需要去处理所有这些事情。

sentences.en: But even more than the Turk, his prime responsibility is an even more stressful one, and that is to coordinate with the French.
sentences.zh: 但比土耳其人更甚的是，他的首要责任是一项压力更大的任务，那就是与法国人进行协调。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a perennial problem for British armies from this point onwards, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从这时起，这一直是英国军队挥之不去的问题，不是吗？

sentences.en: That ultimately, they would much rather be fighting against the French.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，他们其实更愿意跟法国人打仗。

sentences.en: But because of unfortunate diplomatic circumstances, they have to fight alongside them.
sentences.zh: 但由于不幸的外交环境，他们不得不并肩作战。

sentences.en: So if you remember in 1914, there had, you know, when the British soldiers arrived, the British expeditionary force,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你还记得1914年，当英国士兵到达时，也就是英国远征军，

sentences.en: some of them had to be restrained from attacking their allies forthwith.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有些人必须被克制住，才没有直接攻击他们的盟友。

sentences.en: Well, it's the same is true of Raglan.
sentences.zh: 好吧，拉格兰也是如此。

sentences.en: Well, Raglan's been fighting the French all his life, presumably.
sentences.zh: 好吧，拉格兰大概一辈子都在跟法国人打仗。

sentences.en: Yeah, his whole life.
sentences.zh: 是的，他的一生。

sentences.en: He's either been fighting them or preparing to fight them.
sentences.zh: 他要么在跟他们打仗，要么在准备跟他们打仗。

sentences.en: And actually, we mentioned in the previous episode how when Napoleon sees his power, there's a massive war scare in Britain, and they start kind of preparing for a French attack.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们在上一集里提到过，当拿破仑掌握权力时，英国引发了巨大的战争恐慌，他们开始着手准备应对法国的进攻。

sentences.en: The guy put in charge of that was Raglan.
sentences.zh: 负责这件事的人就是拉格兰。

sentences.en: He'd spent the summer of 1852.
sentences.zh: 他度过了1852年的夏天。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, that is the year before the French and British are sending their flotillas to Constantinople.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，那是法国和英国向君士坦丁堡派遣舰队的前一年。

sentences.en: He'd been spending preparing, readying the defences of London against the suspected attack by the French.
sentences.zh: 他一直在筹备，加强伦敦的防御，以防范法国人可能发动的进攻。

sentences.en: So for Raglan, the French are the natural enemy, and he will sometimes forget who he's meant to be fighting and confuse his staff by referring to the enemy, not as the Russians,
sentences.zh: 因此对拉格兰来说，法国人是天然的敌人，他有时会忘记自己本该和谁作战，并把敌人不称作俄国人，反而弄糊涂了他的参谋人员，

sentences.en: but as the French.
sentences.zh: 而是称作法国人。

sentences.en: So he will say, send troops up and attack the French.
sentences.zh: 所以他会说，派军队上去进攻法国人。

sentences.en: And, you know, it causes embarrassment and it becomes notorious.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这令人尴尬并变得人尽皆知。

sentences.en: And this is often used to suggest that Raglan was either senile or hopelessly out of his depth.
sentences.zh: 这经常被用来暗示拉格兰要么老态龙钟，要么完全无能为力、不知所措。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, this is not the case, because we've said that Raglan is a natural diplomat.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你知道，事实并非如此，因为我们说过拉格兰是一位天生的外交官。

sentences.en: He also has perfect French.
sentences.zh: 他的法语也说得极好。

sentences.en: So he had served Wellington after Waterloo had been the British ambassador in Paris and Raglan had been with him.
sentences.zh: 滑铁卢战役后，他曾担任惠灵顿的随从，后来担任英国驻巴黎大使，拉格兰一直陪伴在他身边。

sentences.en: So he had years in Paris and knew France well, speaks French very well.
sentences.zh: 所以他在巴黎度过了多年，对法国很了解，法语说得非常好。

sentences.en: He's not an idiot.
sentences.zh: 他可不是个笨蛋。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, it's understandable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，这其实是可以理解的。

sentences.en: And in fact, on the 11th of April, he arrives in Paris and he meets with Napoleon III and he's greeted with immense enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在4月11日，他抵达巴黎，见到了拿破仑三世，受到了极大的热情欢迎。

sentences.en: There is one voice that sees him and shouts out, you know, you lost your arm at Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 有一个声音看到他并大喊道，你知道的，你在滑铁卢失去了一条胳膊。

sentences.en: Ha, ha, ha.
sentences.zh: 哈哈哈。

sentences.en: But that's the only negative comment.
sentences.zh: 但那是唯一的负面评论。

sentences.en: Everyone else is shouting, vive Longleterre.
sentences.zh: 其他所有人都在高喊，法兰西万岁（Vive l'Angleterre）。

sentences.en: It's all great.
sentences.zh: 一切都好极了。

sentences.en: And he has fruitful meetings with his French opposite number.
sentences.zh: 他与他的法国同行进行了富有成效的会晤。

sentences.en: So the commander in chief of the French army.
sentences.zh: 也就是法国军队的总司令。

sentences.en: And this is a chap called Le Roy de Saint-Arnaud.
sentences.zh: 这是一个叫勒鲁瓦·德·圣阿尔诺的家伙。

sentences.en: Raglan and his staff are not entirely convinced by him.
sentences.zh: 拉格兰和他的参谋人员对他并不是完全信服。

sentences.en: So one of them describes him as a strange flighty fellow and one it will not do to take it his word.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一人将他描述为一个奇怪而反复无常的家伙，一个不能轻信其言的人。

sentences.en: Well, if they don't like a Glasgow carpenter's son, this guy is something else, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果他们不喜欢格拉斯哥木匠的儿子，这家伙可就完全是另一回事了，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, the snobbery is not surprising because as a young man, Sant'Arnaud had worked in London.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这种势利并不令人意外，因为年轻时的圣阿尔诺曾在伦敦生活过。

sentences.en: So Saul David in his biography of Cardigan says that he lived among the prostitutes and pimps of Drury Lane.
sentences.zh: 索尔·戴维在他为卡迪根写的传记中说，他曾混迹于德鲁里巷的妓女和皮条客之间。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And Edward Shawcross, who appeared on our show about Emperor Maximilian in Mexico, he's got a fantastic biography of Napoleon III out.
sentences.zh: 爱德华·肖克罗斯曾做客我们关于墨西哥皇帝马克西米利安的节目，他出版了一本关于拿破仑三世的出色传记。

sentences.en: And he talks about Sant'Arnaud in some detail and says that in London, he'd worked as a fencing coach, dance instructor, poet, violinist, singer and billiards hustler.
sentences.zh: 他在书中详细谈到了圣阿尔诺，并说他在伦敦曾当过击剑教练、舞蹈指导、诗人、小提琴手、歌手和台球骗子。

sentences.en: Oh, my God, how common.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪，多么低俗。

sentences.en: Not the kind of curriculum vitae to impress a British aristocrat.
sentences.zh: 这可不是能给英国贵族留下深刻印象的履历。

sentences.en: Although the positive is that he does speak English.
sentences.zh: 尽管积极的一面是他确实会说英语。

sentences.en: So you've got Raglan speaking French.
sentences.zh: 所以拉格兰会说法语。

sentences.en: You've got Sant'Arnaud speaking English.
sentences.zh: 圣阿尔诺会说英语。

sentences.en: So actually, that's quite good.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，这挺不错的。

sentences.en: Now, Sant'Arnaud is a very hardcore military figure because he'd spent years with the Foreign Legion in Algeria.
sentences.zh: 现在，圣阿尔诺是一个非常强硬的军事人物，因为他在阿尔及利亚的外籍军团度过了多年。

sentences.en: You know, he knows what it is to massacre an innocent village full of civilians.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他深知屠杀一个充满平民的无辜村庄是什么滋味。

sentences.en: He's been there and done the hard yards.
sentences.zh: 他经历过并熬过了那些艰难困苦。

sentences.en: He's experienced that.
sentences.zh: 他对此很有经验。

sentences.en: But he's not only a pretty brutal man, I think, he's also very slippery and very difficult.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，他不仅是个相当残暴的人，而且非常滑头、难以对付。

sentences.en: He loves the scam.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢搞诡计。

sentences.en: He's massively corrupt.
sentences.zh: 他极度腐败。

sentences.en: Lots on the British high staff suspect that he would, for instance, sell secrets to the Russians.
sentences.zh: 英国高级参谋部中的许多人怀疑他会，比如说，向俄国人出售秘密。

sentences.en: I mean, this is not the case.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实并非如此。

sentences.en: But he does have a pretty dark reputation as a kind of an operator.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个善于钻营的人，他确实有着相当黑暗的名声。

sentences.en: And basically, the reason that he's got the command is that he had backed Napoleon's coup.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他能获得这个指挥权的原因是他曾支持拿破仑的政变。

sentences.en: And so he's Napoleon's placeman.
sentences.zh: 所以他是拿破仑的心腹。

sentences.en: And also, he wants the supreme command over the British as well as the French, which is not something that Raglan is prepared to see to him.
sentences.zh: 而且，他还想要对英军和法军的最高指挥权，这并不是拉格兰准备向他妥协的事情。

sentences.en: There's one other thing about Sant'Arnaud that Raglan finds unsettling.
sentences.zh: 关于圣阿尔诺，还有一件事让拉格兰感到不安。

sentences.en: And this is that he doesn't seem particularly well-man.
sentences.zh: 那就是他似乎身体状况不太好。

sentences.en: He has very violent intestinal complaints.
sentences.zh: 他有非常严重的肠胃疾病。

sentences.en: So they'll be chatting about gun emplacements or something.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能正在讨论炮兵阵地之类的事情。

sentences.en: And then he'll suddenly go, oh, and cramp up and bend over.
sentences.zh: 然后他会突然说，哦，然后抽筋并弯下腰去。

sentences.en: OK, well.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: And, you know, so that's just something for the listener to bear in mind.
sentences.zh: 所以，这只是听众需要记住的一点。

sentences.en: That, you know, it's kind of bad stomach.
sentences.zh: 就是那种胃不太好。

sentences.en: So how does Raglan handle him?
sentences.zh: 那么拉格兰该如何应付他呢？

sentences.en: Well, Raglan is an actually courteous man.
sentences.zh: 嗯，拉格兰实际上是个彬彬有礼的人。

sentences.en: He's got flawless French, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 他法语流利，等等等等。

sentences.en: And he proves more than capable of handling this former dancing teacher in the streets of Drury Lane.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他完全有能力应付这位曾在德鲁里巷街头当过舞蹈教师的家伙。

sentences.en: So Raglan manages to dead bat Sant'Arnaud's demands that he be made commander-in-chief.
sentences.zh: 因此，拉格兰成功地顶住了圣阿尔诺关于让他担任总司令的要求。

sentences.en: He hasn't said that he won't recognise Sant'Arnaud as C&C.
sentences.zh: 他并没有说他不承认圣阿尔诺为总司令。

sentences.en: But has he said that he will?
sentences.zh: 但他有没有说他会承认呢？

sentences.en: He hasn't said that he will.
sentences.zh: 他并没有说他会。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确切地说。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确切地说。

sentences.en: But basically what he's agreed is that Britain will supply the majority of the fleet.
sentences.zh: 但基本上他同意的是，英国将提供大部分舰队。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the Navy is Britain's strength.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，海军是英国的强项。

sentences.en: And France will supply the majority of the land forces.
sentences.zh: 而法国将提供大部分陆军力量。

sentences.en: There is one proviso to that.
sentences.zh: 对此有一个附加条件。

sentences.en: The British will supply the cavalry.
sentences.zh: 英国将提供骑兵。

sentences.en: And the reason for this is that the British have much better transport ships than the French do.
sentences.zh: 这样做的原因是英国拥有比法国好得多的运输船。

sentences.en: So you need to, you know, to take horses and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以你需要，你知道的，用来运送马匹等等。

sentences.en: And this, of course, does place a premium on the quality of the cavalry commanders.
sentences.zh: 当然，这自然对骑兵指挥官的素质提出了很高的要求。

sentences.en: Because if the British are the only ones with cavalry, and the Balkans are, you know, lateral cavalry country, then it matters that you have competent commanders in charge of them.
sentences.zh: 因为如果英国是唯一拥有骑兵的一方，而巴尔干半岛又是那种适合骑兵作战的地形，那么由称职的指挥官来掌管他们就至关重要了。

sentences.en: So last time we met the bloke who you said was going to be given the overall command of the cavalry,
sentences.zh: 所以上次我们遇到了那个你说是被指定担任骑兵总指挥的人，

sentences.en: and that was Lord Lucan, who's an irascible, charmless, difficult, unlovable man, isn't he, Lord Lucan?
sentences.zh: 那就是卢卡恩勋爵，他是一个暴躁、毫无魅力、难以相处、令人讨厌的人，对吧，卢卡恩勋爵？

sentences.en: Yes, but he is brave and conscientious and contemptuous of his own comforts.
sentences.zh: 是的，但他很勇敢、尽责，并且对自己的舒适生活不屑一顾。

sentences.en: And he had served on the staff of a Russian general in the campaign against the Turks and the Balkans.
sentences.zh: 他曾在巴尔干半岛针对土耳其人的战役中担任过某位俄国将军的参谋。

sentences.en: So he's an old Balkan hand.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个老巴尔干通。

sentences.en: He's an old Balkan hand like you.
sentences.zh: 他就像你一样是个老巴尔干通。

sentences.en: But as you say, people don't warm to him.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所说，人们并不喜欢他。

sentences.en: And he works really, really hard, but to kind of fruitless effect.
sentences.zh: 他工作非常非常努力，但却没什么成效。

sentences.en: And people find him fractious and arrogant and unable to see the big picture for the details.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得他顽固、傲慢，只见树木不见森林。

sentences.en: He's the kind of the Kendall Roy of the British Army.
sentences.zh: 他可以说是英军里的肯德尔·罗伊。

sentences.en: My word.
sentences.zh: 我的天呐。

sentences.en: He aspires, but he never quite gets there.
sentences.zh: 他满怀雄心，却总是差那么一点。

sentences.en: He never quite pulls it off.
sentences.zh: 他总也干不出什么名堂。

sentences.en: But this is the guy who's been appointed head of the British cavalry on the 21st of February.
sentences.zh: 但就是这个人，在2月21日被任命为英国骑兵司令。

sentences.en: And now who are going to be his deputies?
sentences.zh: 那么谁将是他的副手呢？

sentences.en: These are appointed on the 1st of April, April Fool's Day.
sentences.zh: 这些任命是在4月1日，愚人节那天宣布的。

sentences.en: So, you know, is this a joke or is it not?
sentences.zh: 所以，这到底是个笑话还是认真的？

sentences.en: We will see.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: So the cavalry are divided into two brigades, each one consisting of five wedgements.
sentences.zh: 骑兵被分为两个旅，每个旅包含五个团。

sentences.en: And these wedgements in turn comprise some 300 men.
sentences.zh: 这些团又各自包含大约300名士兵。

sentences.en: And the 1st brigade consists of heavy cavalry.
sentences.zh: 第一旅由重骑兵组成。

sentences.en: So large horses, large recruits, heavy savers, brass helmets.
sentences.zh: 所以马匹高大，新兵魁梧，配备重型马刀和黄铜头盔。

sentences.en: They're a shock force.
sentences.zh: 他们是一支突击力量。

sentences.en: They can be used to break enemy formations, cavalry or infantry.
sentences.zh: 他们可以用来冲破敌人的阵型，无论是骑兵还是步兵。

sentences.en: And at Waterloo, three of the five regiments who were constituting the heavy brigade had been a part of the famous Union Brigade, which we mentioned in the previous episode.
sentences.zh: 在滑铁卢战役中，构成重骑兵旅的五个团中有三个曾属于著名的“联合旅”，我们在上一集里提到过。

sentences.en: Union Brigade, because it consists of an English, a Scottish and an Irish regiment.
sentences.zh: 之所以叫联合旅，是因为它由一个英格兰团、一个苏格兰团和一个爱尔兰团组成。

sentences.en: And it had broken a French infantry attack and taken two eagles at Waterloo.
sentences.zh: 它曾在滑铁卢冲垮了法军的步兵进攻，并缴获了两面鹰旗。

sentences.en: And these three regiments were the 1st Royal Dragoons, the 2nd Dragoons, who were the Scots Greys.
sentences.zh: 这三个团是皇家龙骑兵第一团、第二龙骑兵团（即苏格兰灰马团）。

sentences.en: So there's the famous painting by Lady Butler in the 1880s, I think it was done.
sentences.zh: 巴特勒夫人（Lady Butler）在19世纪80年代创作过一幅著名的画作，我想就是那时候画的。

sentences.en: And the 6th Dragoons, who were the Inniskillings.
sentences.zh: 还有第六龙骑兵团，也就是恩尼斯基林团。

sentences.en: So they're the Irish.
sentences.zh: 所以他们是爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: So they have this glorious history.
sentences.zh: 他们有着这样一段光荣的历史。

sentences.en: You know, they know their regimental history.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们了解自己团的历史。

sentences.en: They are looking forward after four decades to reprising that history and enjoying a heroic charge and seeing off the enemy.
sentences.zh: 在经历了四十年后，他们期盼着重现那段历史，享受一次英雄般的冲锋，并消灭敌人。

sentences.en: So that's the heavy brigade.
sentences.zh: 这就是重骑兵旅。

sentences.en: And the man in charge of the heavy brigade, who's that?
sentences.zh: 那么，统领重骑兵旅的人是谁呢？

sentences.en: He is a chap called Brigadier General Sir James Scarlet.
sentences.zh: 他是一个叫詹姆斯·斯嘉丽爵士的准将。

sentences.en: And he's Scarlet by name and Scarlet by nature, because he has a bright red face.
sentences.zh: 他不仅名字叫斯嘉丽（意为猩红），连脾气也像斯嘉丽，因为他有一张通红的脸。

sentences.en: He's very stout.
sentences.zh: 他身材非常健硕。

sentences.en: He has tremendously white whiskers.
sentences.zh: 他有着极其显眼的白色络腮胡。

sentences.en: He has no experience for combat.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何实战经验。

sentences.en: So he's a chap who's bought his own commission again.
sentences.zh: 所以他也是一个花钱买官的人。

sentences.en: But unlike other commanders on the expedition, he is aware of the fact that this isn't perhaps ideal preparation.
sentences.zh: 但与远征军中的其他指挥官不同，他很清楚这或许并不是最理想的备战方式。

sentences.en: And so he's made a point of surrounding himself by Indian officers, people who have had combat experience.
sentences.zh: 因此，他特意在身边安插了许多曾在印度服役、有过实战经验的军官。

sentences.en: And he's a very jolly and unassuming man.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常开朗、平易近人的人。

sentences.en: And over the course of the war, he will come to be greatly loved by the men in the heavy brigade.
sentences.zh: 在战争期间，他将深受重骑兵旅官兵的爱戴。

sentences.en: And they kind of describe him as a good, kind old fellow.
sentences.zh: 他们把他描述为一个善良、亲切的老好人。

sentences.en: Oh, he sounds great.
sentences.zh: 哦，听起来真不错。

sentences.en: Now, that's the heavy brigade.
sentences.zh: 好了，这就是重骑兵旅。

sentences.en: Good, kind old fellow.
sentences.zh: 善良、亲切的老好人。

sentences.en: Is the man in charge of the light brigade equally well-loved, sort of an avuncular and charming and Father Christmas-like?
sentences.zh: 统领轻骑兵旅的那个人也同样备受喜爱吗？他是不是那种慈祥、迷人、像圣诞老人一样的人？

sentences.en: Well, we'll come to whether he's loved, but he's certainly not popular and he's certainly not avuncular and he's certainly nothing like Father Christmas.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们等会儿再讨论他是否受欢迎，但他绝对谈不上讨人喜欢，也绝不慈祥，更一点都不像圣诞老人。

sentences.en: And this is someone that we met in the previous episode, and this is Lord Cardigan.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们在上一集里介绍过的人，卡迪根伯爵。

sentences.en: So he is a man who's perpetually falling out with his own officers, court-martialing them, you know, fighting duels with them, shooting them in the back,
sentences.zh: 他是一个总是与自己的军官闹翻、送他们上军事法庭、和他们决斗、甚至在背后放冷枪的人……

sentences.en: having rows over black bottles.
sentences.zh: 因为黑酒瓶的事情跟人吵架。

sentences.en: I was about to say, you take a black bottle to the Crimea and you're in massive trouble.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，你要是带个黑酒瓶去克里米亚，那你可就大难临头了。

sentences.en: And on top of that, Cardigan and Lucan, as we also mentioned in the previous episode, detest each other.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，正如我们在上一集也提到过的，卡迪根和卢肯互相痛恨对方。

sentences.en: So Lucan is married to Cardigan's younger sister and they've fallen out badly.
sentences.zh: 卢肯娶了卡迪根的小妹妹，结果两人闹得很僵。

sentences.en: And so Cardigan is taking his sister's side.
sentences.zh: 因此卡迪根一直站在他妹妹这一边。

sentences.en: And so the big question is, how will Cardigan take to having Lord Lucan as his commanding officer?
sentences.zh: 所以最大的问题是，卡迪根会如何看待卢肯伯爵成为他的直属长官？

sentences.en: And of course, how will Lucan manage having a subordinate as tricky and pig-headed as Cardigan?
sentences.zh: 当然，卢肯又将如何管束像卡迪根这样棘手且顽固的下属？

sentences.en: These are questions that concern pretty much everyone in the army.
sentences.zh: 这些问题几乎是军中所有人都关心的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, absolutely mad to appoint these two men, by the way.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我是说，任命这两个人简直疯狂透顶。

sentences.en: A typical response is that given by an officer in the 4th Light Dragoon, so one of the regiments in the Light Brigade.
sentences.zh: 一个典型的反应来自第四轻骑兵团的一名军官，也就是轻骑兵旅的其中一个团。

sentences.en: This is a chap called Captain Henry Portal.
sentences.zh: 这人叫亨利·波特尔上尉。

sentences.en: And Portal wrote, two bigger fools could not be pulled out of the British army.
sentences.zh: 波特尔写道，整个英国军队里也找不出比这俩更大的蠢货了。

sentences.en: So that's the view from the, you know, from the officer class.
sentences.zh: 这就是来自军官阶层的看法。

sentences.en: And even Raglan, who is actually a family friend of Cardigan's, they know each other quite well.
sentences.zh: 甚至连拉格伦——他实际上是卡迪根的家族朋友，两人相当熟悉——

sentences.en: I mean, even he writes to Harding and says, Cardigan and Lucan together, you really sure?
sentences.zh: 我是说，连他都写信给哈丁说：“卡迪根和卢肯搭档，你们真的确定吗？”

sentences.en: I mean, you know, trouble.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这绝对会惹麻烦。

sentences.en: But Harding says, no, no, Cardigan is the man for the job.
sentences.zh: 但哈丁却说：“不，不，卡迪根就是胜任此职的最佳人选。”

sentences.en: So people are really, you know, if Harding is this kind of competent figure that we've been portraying, how on earth has he ever appointed Cardigan to this post?
sentences.zh: 所以大家真的很纳闷，如果哈丁是我们一直在描述的那种精明能干的人物，他到底怎么会把卡迪根任命到这个岗位上？

sentences.en: And I think the simple truth is that he actually rates Carding pretty highly as a commander.
sentences.zh: 我想最简单的真相是，他实际上对卡迪根作为指挥官的能力评价相当高。

sentences.en: Now, it is true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: We, in the previous episode, we dwelt on his tendency to fall out with his officers.
sentences.zh: 我们在上一集里曾详细说过他容易跟军官闹翻的倾向。

sentences.en: Yes, arresting them for wearing the wrong shoes or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为穿错鞋子之类的琐事就把他们关禁闭。

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: But I think that Harding feels that the reason for this is because Cardigan's standards of smartness and discipline are very, very high.
sentences.zh: 但我想哈丁觉得，之所以会这样，是因为卡迪根对整洁和纪律的要求非常、非常高。

sentences.en: And it is absolutely the case that the regiment that Cardigan had been commanding, the 11th Hussars, you know, they are the most brilliant in the whole British cavalry.
sentences.zh: 而且事实确实如此，卡迪根曾经指挥过的那个团，即第11轻骑兵团，可以说是整个英国骑兵中最出色的。

sentences.en: They're the best dressed.
sentences.zh: 他们的军服最好看。

sentences.en: They're the best equipped.
sentences.zh: 他们的装备最精良。

sentences.en: They're the best and most exactingly trained.
sentences.zh: 他们接受的训练最好、最严苛。

sentences.en: And you ask, was he loved?
sentences.zh: 你可能会问，他受人爱戴吗？

sentences.en: I mean, he's definitely not loved by his officers.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他绝对不受手下军官的爱戴。

sentences.en: But he does seem to have been, if not loved, then kind of admired by the troopers, by the men who, you know,
sentences.zh: 但对于普通士兵来说，即使谈不上爱戴，也似乎颇受钦佩——这些士兵……

sentences.en: are from much poorer background than the officers and are being lavished with these pink pants and fine tailoring from Savile Row and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们的出身比军官穷得多，却穿着萨维尔街定制的高档剪裁制服和粉红马裤。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So they actually seem to have thought Cardigan was a great man to have in charge of them.
sentences.zh: 所以他们实际上觉得卡迪根是个带领他们的绝佳人选。

sentences.en: Well, they love a plunger, don't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们就喜欢有魄力的赌徒，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: They admire a bit of dash and swagger.
sentences.zh: 他们崇拜那种带点冲劲和傲气的人。

sentences.en: So Cardigan, I think, is, I mean, he is a very high Tory.
sentences.zh: 所以卡迪根，我认为，他是一个坚定的托利党人。

sentences.en: So on his estate, the estate workers love him.
sentences.zh: 所以在他的领地上，庄园工人们都很爱戴他。

sentences.en: He looks out for them.
sentences.zh: 他很关照他们。

sentences.en: The people who don't love him are the, you know, the rector or the local lawyer or whatever who Cardigan treats with utter contempt.
sentences.zh: 唯独不爱戴他的是那些牧师、当地律师之类的人，卡迪根对这些人充满了极度的鄙视。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But as a high Tory, Cardigan despises Indian officers.
sentences.zh: 但作为一名坚定的托利党人，卡迪根鄙视印度军官。

sentences.en: But the common man, the common British trooper, we love the British trooper.
sentences.zh: 然而普通人，普通的英国骑兵——我们太爱英国骑兵了。

sentences.en: Yeah, completely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: So in 1840, when it was kind of the eye of the storm, the black bottle and all of that,
sentences.zh: 所以在1840年，正值风口浪尖、黑酒瓶事件闹得沸沸扬扬之时……

sentences.en: wrote to the Naval and Military Gazette to condemn Cardigan's treatment by the press and praised him as one of the best colonels in the British army ever alive to the interests and éclat of his regiment.
sentences.zh: 有人写信给《海军与军事公报》，谴责媒体对卡迪根的处理方式，并赞扬他是英国军队中最优秀的指挥官之一，时刻关注着其团队的利益和荣誉。

sentences.en: And the letter went on to praise Cardigan for his hard work, for his attention to detail and the lavish spending on the regiment.
sentences.zh: 信中接着赞扬了卡迪根的辛勤工作、对细节的一丝不苟以及对团队的大手笔投入。

sentences.en: And it finished, for he is deservedly respected, a good man who not a soldier under him would follow into action with confidence,
sentences.zh: 信的结尾写道：“因此他理应受到尊敬，他是一个好人，没有一个士兵会不怀着信心追随他投入战斗……”

sentences.en: nor hesitate a moment to shield from danger by his own body in the battlefield.
sentences.zh: “也绝不会在战场上有片刻犹豫，不愿用自己的身躯为他挡住危险。”

sentences.en: And you might think, oh, is this something that Cardigan himself wrote?
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，哦，这是卡迪根自己写的吗？

sentences.en: But I don't think it is because, as saw David in his tremendous biography of Cardigan, which has the brilliant title of The Homicidal Earl, he says,
